title: Square-zero algebraic-space thickenings: realization and maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $B$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $f:X\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A first-order thickening $X\hookrightarrow X'$ means a closed immersion, checked on etale scheme charts [def-weil-closed-immersion], defined by an ideal of square zero, and inducing the same underlying topological space. Pullback identifies the small etale sites of $X'$ and $X$. Let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Every exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal O_X\to0$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-algebras, $p$ is an algebra map, and $i(\mathcal G)$ is an ideal of square zero with its prescribed $\mathcal O_X$-module structure, is realized by a first-order thickening $X\hookrightarrow X'$ over $B$ together with $\mathcal O_{X'}\cong\mathcal A$ compatible with $p$ and $i$. This realization is unique up to the unique isomorphism inducing the specified isomorphism of extensions. More generally, for first-order thickenings $X\hookrightarrow X'$ and $Y\hookrightarrow Y'$ over $B$ and a $B$-morphism $g:X\to Y$, every map of ring sheaves $\alpha:g^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'}\to\mathcal O_{X'}$ over $B$, reducing to $g^\sharp:g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$, is induced by a unique $B$-morphism $g':X'\to Y'$ lifting $g$. Here inverse images use the identified small etale topoi, and all module sheaves and exact sequences have the meaning of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: First prove the site assertion independently of the extension. A first-order thickening $i:X\hookrightarrow X'$ is a closed immersion of schemes after pullback to an etale scheme atlas of $X'$, so [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] makes $i$ representable with every scheme base change a closed immersion. Together with the homeomorphism $|X|\to|X'|$ it is a thickening in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-thickening-etale-scheme-equivalence], which gives the equivalence $V'\mapsto V=V'\times_{X'}X$ from etale scheme objects over $X'$ to etale scheme objects over $X$, with all morphisms over the base. Coverings correspond: by [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change] each projection $V\to V'$ is again a thickening, hence a homeomorphism on point spaces, so a family $\{V'_j\to V'\}$ is jointly surjective if and only if $\{V_j\to V\}$ is. Thus pullback identifies the small etale sites of $X'$ and $X$, and hence their sheaf topoi.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), proof by scheme charts and etale presentation; Tag 05ZN for maps; Tag 05ZS for the site equivalence.

proof.text: Forget the base structure temporarily: by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] regard $X$, $B$ and the spaces below as algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with the same etale scheme charts and small etale ringed sites. Choose an etale scheme atlas $U\to X$ and its kernel pair $R=U\times_XU$, as supplied by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Restrict the extension to the scheme objects $U,R$ and their iterated fibre products. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-square-zero-chart-construction] these give schemes $U^+,R^+$, maps $s^+,t^+:R^+\to U^+$ that are etale, and functorial lifts of the diagonal, inverse and composition. The same node identifies $R^+\times_{U^+}R^+$ with the lift of $R\times_UR$. Their groupoid identities follow from functoriality. This is an equivalence relation: $R^+\to U^+\times U^+$ is a monomorphism since $s^+$ is etale, hence unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified] and the reduction $R\to U\times U$ is a monomorphism. Explicitly, for two maps from a test scheme to $R^+$ with equal source and target, restrict to the square-zero closed subscheme pulled back from $U\subset U^+$; on that subscheme the two maps agree by the monomorphism for $R$, and uniqueness of etale lifting makes them equal on the test scheme.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), proof by scheme charts and etale presentation; Tag 05ZN for maps; Tag 05ZS for the site equivalence.

proof.text: Form the sheaf quotient $X^+=U^+/R^+$ using [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. It is an algebraic space with atlas $U^+$ and kernel pair $R^+$. The induced map $X=U/R\to X^+$ pulls back along $U^+\to X^+$ to $U\hookrightarrow U^+$. To check this identity, locally lift a section of $X$ to $U$; a section of its fibre product with $U^+$ is then a pair consisting of that lift and an element of $U^+$ joined by an arrow in $R^+$. Since $(s^+)^{-1}(U)=R$, this arrow is in $R$, and its target is in $U$. Changes of the local lift are precisely arrows in $R$, giving the stated identification by the quotient's kernel-pair formula. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] to the atlas $U^+$ and this closed immersion $U\to U^+$. Thus $X\hookrightarrow X^+$ is a closed immersion. Its ideal is square-zero and it is a homeomorphism on point spaces since these assertions hold on the atlas $U^+$. This is a first-order thickening.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), proof by scheme charts and etale presentation; Tag 05ZN for maps; Tag 05ZS for the site equivalence.

proof.text: Use step 1 to view $\mathcal O_{X^+}$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-square-zero-chart-construction], its restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ is canonically $\mathcal A|_U$, and the two identifications agree after restriction to $R_{\mathrm{et}}$, since all chart maps were made from the restriction maps of $\mathcal A$. They therefore glue uniquely to $\gamma:\mathcal O_{X^+}\simeq\mathcal A$. Concretely, for any $W\to X$ restrict sections to the cover $W\times_XU\to W$; the two values on $W\times_XR$ agree, so the equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] defines a unique image section on $W$. Apply the same construction to the inverse chart isomorphisms to obtain the inverse to $\gamma$. The formulas commute with restriction, ring operations, quotient and kernel inclusion because they do on that cover.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), proof by scheme charts and etale presentation; Tag 05ZN for maps; Tag 05ZS for the site equivalence.

proof.text: For the maps clause use the site equivalences in step 1 to view $(g_{\mathrm{et}},\alpha)$ as a morphism of ringed topoi for $X',Y'$. Regard $X',Y'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with unchanged small etale ringed sites [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers], as the cited reconstruction requires. Check locality directly using [lem-sfb-space-locally-ringed-etale-topos-reconstruction]. Locally represent sections of an inverse-image sheaf by sections on its defining site. A section $b$ of $g^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'}$ whose image under $\alpha$ is invertible has reduction $\bar b$ invertible in $g^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$: the reduced morphism is $g$, whose ringed-topos map is local by the cited statement. Hence $b$ is locally invertible as well. Indeed, lift an inverse of $\bar b$ locally through the surjective quotient; if $bc=1+j$ with $j$ in its square-zero kernel, then $c(1-j)$ is an inverse for $b$. This computation also applies after inverse image: a geometric inverse image preserves finite limits and colimits, hence the quotient is still locally surjective and its kernel square-zero. Every ring map preserves invertibility, so the required units square is cartesian. Reconstruction therefore gives a unique space morphism $g':X'\to Y'$ inducing this ringed-topos map, with its specified identification.

The composites $g'\circ i_X$ and $i_Y\circ g$ induce the same ringed-topos morphism: after the canonical site identifications their ring maps agree by $p_X\alpha=g^\sharp g^{-1}p_Y$, the assumed reduction square. Faithfulness in [lem-sfb-space-locally-ringed-etale-topos-reconstruction] makes these space morphisms equal. If $q_X:X'\to B$ and $q_Y:Y'\to B$ are the structure maps, the inverse-image functors for $q_Y\circ g'$ and $q_X$ agree because they reduce to those of the equality $q_Y|_Y\circ g=q_X|_X$. Their ring maps agree because $\alpha$ is a map over $B$. Faithfulness again gives $q_Y\circ g'=q_X$, so $g'$ is over $B$, hence compatible with the maps to $S$ and so a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers]. Any other lift inducing $\alpha$ gives the same ringed-topos morphism; reconstruction's uniqueness gives the same $g'$. This proves the general maps clause without assuming that $g$ is the identity.

The construction so far gives an absolute algebraic space $X^+$. Its isomorphism $\gamma$ gives the ring map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B\to\mathcal O_{X^+}$ reducing to $f^\sharp$. Apply the maps assertion proved in steps 5 and 6 over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with reduced map $f:X\to B$ and the identity thickening $B\subset B$. This gives $X^+\to B$ extending $f$. By [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] the composite $X^+\to B\to S$ makes $X^+$ an algebraic space over $S$ with the same small etale ringed site, and $X\hookrightarrow X^+\to B$ are then morphisms over $S$. Identify the thickening's ideal with $\mathcal G$ using $\gamma$ and $i^{-1}$ on the quotient kernel; its induced module structure is the prescribed one because all actions are quotient multiplication. Hence $\gamma$ respects $p$, $i$ and the base algebra structure.

source.place: Tag 05ZT (lemma-first-order-thickening), proof by scheme charts and etale presentation; Tag 05ZN for maps; Tag 05ZS for the site equivalence.

proof.text: Given two realizations and a specified isomorphism of extensions, its induced ring-sheaf isomorphism and inverse both reduce to $\mathrm{id}_X$ and are over $B$. The maps assertion of steps 5 and 6 therefore supplies unique morphisms of thickenings in opposite directions. Each composite induces the identity ring map; the uniqueness in that same assertion forces each composite to be the identity. This gives precisely the unique isomorphism compatible with the specified isomorphism of extensions.
